# hush_custom_api_application (Resource)

A custom API app: a REST API described here so `hush_api_application` can create applications from it (with `app_catalog_id` set to this resource's `app_catalog_id`), each serving its enabled tools to agents. Changes to the address, headers, credential and tools carry over to every application created from it. It cannot be destroyed while an application still uses it.

Detecting the tools from the OpenAPI spec and optimizing them run in the console, not here: detect or optimize there, review the tools, then write them as `tool` blocks (`terraform import` reads them back, `operation_id` included).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A REST API with two tools written by hand. To use the tools detected from
# spec_url instead, create the app without tool blocks, detect and review them
# in the console, then import it to copy them here, operation_id included.
# Create applications from it with
# app_catalog_id = hush_custom_api_application.billing.app_catalog_id.
resource "hush_custom_api_application" "billing" {
  name         = "billing"
  display_name = "Billing API"
  url          = "https://billing.internal.example.com"
  spec_url     = "https://billing.internal.example.com/openapi.json"

  auth {
    type              = "bearer"
    secret_wo         = var.billing_api_token
    secret_wo_version = "1"
  }

  tool {
    name        = "list_invoices"
    title       = "List invoices"
    description = "List the invoices of a customer"
    type        = "read"
    method      = "GET"
    path        = "/v1/invoices"
    input_schema = jsonencode({
      type = "object"
      properties = {
        query = {
          type       = "object"
          properties = { customer_id = { type = "string" } }
          required   = ["customer_id"]
        }
      }
    })
  }
  tool {
    name    = "void_invoice"
    title   = "Void invoice"
    type    = "destructive"
    method  = "POST"
    path    = "/v1/invoices/{id}/void"
    enabled = false
    input_schema = jsonencode({
      type = "object"
      properties = {
        path = { type = "object", properties = { id = { type = "string" } } }
      }
    })
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `display_name` (String) The name the custom app is shown under.
- `name` (String) The custom app's name: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter or digit, at most 56 characters. It is fixed at creation. heimdall allows 63, but applications are created from 'custom-<name>', which it caps at 63, so a longer name could never have any.
- `url` (String) The API's address. A tool's `path` is taken from its host, not appended to its path.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `auth` (Block List, Max: 1) A fixed credential the gateway presents to the API. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--auth))
- `description` (String) A description of the custom app.
- `headers` (Map of String) Extra HTTP headers the gateway sends with every request to the API. Names the gateway owns (Authorization, Host, Content-Type and the like, and any starting with 'proxy-', 'x-hush-' or 'hush-') are refused.
- `spec_url` (String) The address of the API's OpenAPI spec, which the console detects the tools from.
- `tool` (Block List) A tool the API offers: one operation of it. The blocks replace the app's whole tool list, which agents get the enabled tools of; with none written, whatever the custom app holds (detected in the console, for instance) is left alone. While applications use the app, at least one tool must be enabled. The operation the gateway applies to a tool is set per application, by `tool_operation`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tool))

### Read-Only

- `app_catalog_id` (String) The id an application is created from: the name prefixed with 'custom-'.
- `detect_required` (Boolean) Whether `url` or `spec_url` changed since the tools were last detected.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedblock--auth"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auth`

Required:

- `type` (String) 'bearer' (sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <secret>'), 'basic' (sent as basic auth with `username`), 'header' (sent as header `name`) or 'client_credentials' (an OAuth client, `client_id` with the secret, that the gateway exchanges at `token_url` for access tokens it sends as bearer tokens).

Optional:

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `auth_method` (String) How the client authenticates at the token endpoint, for type 'client_credentials' only: 'basic' (the default, HTTP basic auth) or 'post' (in the form body).
- `client_id` (String) The OAuth client id, for type 'client_credentials' only.
- `name` (String) The header name, for type 'header' only. It cannot be 'Authorization' (use 'bearer' or 'basic') or a name `headers` already sets.
- `scopes` (List of String) The scopes to request, for type 'client_credentials' only.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The token, password, header value or client secret. Stored in Terraform state; prefer secret_wo. The API never returns it.
- `secret_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The token, password, header value or client secret, kept out of Terraform state. Sent when secret_wo_version changes.
- `secret_wo_version` (String) Change to re-send secret_wo. Required with it.
- `token_url` (String) The token endpoint, for type 'client_credentials' only.
- `username` (String) The user name, for type 'basic' only.


<a id="nestedblock--tool"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tool`

Required:

- `method` (String) The HTTP method: 'GET', 'PUT', 'POST', 'DELETE', 'OPTIONS', 'HEAD', 'PATCH' or 'TRACE'.
- `name` (String) The tool's name, up to 128 characters without whitespace.
- `path` (String) The path, from the host of `url`. Its `{placeholders}` must be the path arguments of `input_schema`.
- `type` (String) The tool's class: 'read', 'write' or 'destructive'. Each application applies the class's default operation unless it sets one for the tool.

Optional:

- `content_type` (String) How the body is sent: 'application/json' (the default) or 'application/octet-stream'.
- `description` (String) What the tool does.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether agents get the tool. Defaults to true.
- `input_schema` (String) The tool's arguments as a JSON object schema whose properties are any of 'path', 'query', 'header' and 'body', each an object schema of its arguments. Use `jsonencode`. Defaults to `{"type":"object"}`, no arguments.
- `operation_id` (String) The spec's operationId of a tool detected in the console, which the next detect matches it by, so it can be renamed. Only a tool the app already has can name one, so a new app takes none: create it without, detect, then import. Leave unset for a tool written by hand.
- `title` (String) A short title, up to 64 characters.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the custom app's name, which also reads its tools. The secret is not
# returned by the API, so the next apply sends it again.
terraform import hush_custom_api_application.billing billing
```
